reasons: Claimed status is compliant and no redline or comment was proposed, which is the correct output for a compliant finding.

The cited text supports compliance with the preferred position: professional/workmanlike performance and industry standards (19.1), material conformance of Services and Deliverables to documentation (19.1–19.2), 90 days for Deliverables plus conformance of Hosted Services for the whole subscription term (meeting/exceeding the 12-month software benchmark), compliance with Applicable Law and no malicious code (19.3), and a repair/replace/re-perform-then-refund remedy that is expressly non-exclusive for key claim types (19.4).

The disclaimer in 19.5 does not swallow the express warranty — it is confined to implied warranties and expressly preserves express warranties, service levels, indemnities and stated remedies — so the 'carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer' element of the rule is already satisfied.
The failed deterministic check is a phrasing artifact: the period is written as 'ninety days' in words rather than digits, so the regex miss is not evidence of a substantive deviation.

The rationale's treatment of the one narrowing (malicious code limited to code 'intentionally introduced by Vendor') as customary and immaterial is a reasonable judgment that does not undermine the compliant classification.
